html:
The Kushan Empire was a state founded by one branch of the Yuezhi nomads in Bactria in the early 1st century CE. At its height it ruled from Central Asia across Afghanistan and Pakistan into the Ganges plain of north India.

The Yuezhi had been driven west from China by the Xiongnu and settled in Bactria in the 2nd century BCE. Around 30 CE Kujula Kadphises united their five branches. His successors pushed south into India. The greatest king, Kanishka, ruled in the 2nd century from Purushapura, modern Peshawar, and Mathura. His exact dates are still argued, and so is much of Kushan chronology.

The empire sat on the hinge of the Silk Road, between Han China, Parthian Iran, Rome and India. That shows in what it left:

  • Gold coins on the Roman standard, with Greek, Iranian, Indian and Buddhist gods.
  • The Buddhist art of Gandhara, which gave the Buddha a human face in a style mixing Greek and Indian forms.
  • Monks who carried Buddhism north over the mountains; Buddhism reached China in these centuries.

The court first wrote in Greek, then in Bactrian, an Iranian language in Greek letters.

In the 3rd century the Sasanian Empire took the western lands and set up Kushano-Sasanian rulers there. Smaller Kushan kings held on in the east until the Gupta Empire rose in north India in the 4th century.
sum: The Kushan Empire was a state founded by one branch of the Yuezhi nomads in Bactria in the early 1st century CE. At its height it ruled from Central Asia across Afghanistan and Pakistan into the Ganges plain of north India.
